# `js/string-content`

**Strings say it the project's way**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Pack** | `@codelaw/rules-js` (npm) · `codelaw-rules-js` (PyPI) |
| **Languages** | JavaScript, JSX, TypeScript, TSX |
| **Turned on by** | no preset — name it in `[rules]` |
| **Severity when named without one** | `error` |
| **Options** | `patterns` |
| **Fix** | `auto` — `codelaw fix` applies it; it never changes what the code does |
| **Stability** | `preview` — runs only with `preview = true` |
| **Since** | 0.5.2 |
| **Ported from** | `eslint-plugin-unicorn/string-content` |

## What it checks

Text the project does not want in a string literal or a template's text is replaced: `patterns = { "\\.\\.\\." = "…" }` turns `"Loading..."` into `"Loading…"`. A key is a regular expression; its value is the replacement, or an object with `suggest` (the replacement), `fix` (`false` makes the edit a suggestion instead of an automatic fix), `caseSensitive` (`false` ignores case) and `message` (which may use `{{match}}` and `{{suggest}}`; the default is ``Prefer `{{suggest}}` over `{{match}}`.``). The first pattern that matches a string decides, and every match in it is replaced. Template text is read between its substitutions, and `gql`, `html`, `sql`, `styled` and `svg` templates, which hold another language, are not read. Behaviour of eslint-plugin-unicorn 79.0.0's rule for JavaScript, read and reimplemented: a string is read as written, so a match that overlaps an escape sequence (`\n`, `\u2019`) is not reported, and the CSS, TOML and YAML halves are other packs' rules; its `selectors` option, which names ESTree nodes, has no equivalent. A pattern that is not a valid regular expression is reported once, on the file's first string.

With no `patterns` set the rule is silent: it reports nothing, not even that the option is missing, and the engine does not run it on a single node. It is in no preset; a project switches it on by setting the option under `[rules]` (or in a `[scope.<name>]` for some files).

In `codelaw.toml`, under `[rules]`: `"js/string-content" = { severity = "warn", options = { patterns = { "\\.\\.\\." = "…" } } }`.

**Why:** Typography, spelling and house style in user-facing strings are a list a project keeps; the rule applies it.

## Configuration

Everything below goes in `codelaw.toml` at the repo root. The same keys work as `[tool.codelaw]` in `pyproject.toml` or `"codelaw"` in `package.json` ([SR-CONFIG](../../../records/0110_config.md)).

### Turn it on

**Install the pack** (`codelaw init` does it for the languages it finds):

```bash
npm install --save-dev @codelaw/rules-js
pip install codelaw-rules-js
```

**No preset turns it on.** Load its pack through any preset (`codelaw:js/recommended` here), then name the rule in `[rules]`:

```toml
preview = true                        # pack rules are preview today
extends = ["codelaw:js/recommended"]

[rules]
"js/string-content" = "error"
```

- **A rule exists only once its pack is loaded** through `extends`; naming it in `[rules]` without that is an unknown rule id (exit 2).
- **Without `preview = true`** the rule is skipped and codelaw warns that it is preview.

### Severity

```toml
[rules]
"js/string-content" = "warn"    # error | warn | info | off
```

- **`error`** fails the run (exit 1) · **`warn`** fails only with `--max-warnings N` · **`info`** never fails · **`off`** turns it off.
- **Naming it with a severity turns it on** even when no preset does.

### Options

| Option | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `patterns` | `object` | `{}` | a regular expression to the text that replaces what it matches: a string, or `{ suggest, fix, caseSensitive, message }` |

**Every option at its default** — a starting point to copy:

```toml
[rules."js/string-content"]
severity = "error"

[rules."js/string-content".options]
patterns = {}
```

**The same, inline, with example values:**

```toml
[rules]
"js/string-content" = { severity = "error", options = { patterns = { "\\\\.\\\\.\\\\." = "…" } } }
```

- **A table without `severity`** changes only the options: the severity stays what a preset or an earlier layer set, and a rule that is off stays off.
- **A list option replaces its default** — copy the default entries you want to keep.
- **An unknown option or a value of the wrong type** stops the run with exit 2 and names the nearest option.

#### `patterns`

*object* · default `{}`

a regular expression to the text that replaces what it matches: a string, or `{ suggest, fix, caseSensitive, message }`

```toml
[rules."js/string-content".options]
patterns = { "\\\\.\\\\.\\\\." = "…" }
```

### Options in action

Each case below is one of the rule's tests (`packs/js/rules/js/string-content.cases.md`): the options, the input, and what codelaw reports.

#### a string

```toml
[rules."js/string-content".options]
patterns = { "\\\\.\\\\.\\\\." = "…" }
```

```js
const loading = "Loading...";
```

**Reports** at `1:17`.

**After `codelaw fix`:**

```js
const loading = "Loading…";
```

#### a template's text

```toml
[rules."js/string-content".options]
patterns = { "\\\\.\\\\.\\\\." = "…" }
```

```js
const text = `Wait...${n}...`;
```

**Reports** at `1:15`, `1:26`.

**After `codelaw fix`:**

```js
const text = `Wait…${n}…`;
```

#### a fix that is only a suggestion

```toml
[rules."js/string-content".options]
patterns = { colour = { suggest = "color", fix = false } }
```

```js
const a = "colour";
```

**Reports** at `1:11`.

#### case does not matter

```toml
[rules."js/string-content".options]
patterns = { colour = { suggest = "color", caseSensitive = false } }
```

```js
const a = "Colour";
```

**Reports** at `1:11`.

**After `codelaw fix`:**

```js
const a = "color";
```

#### the replacement is escaped for its quote

```toml
[rules."js/string-content".options]
patterns = { "\\\\.\\\\.\\\\." = "'" }
```

```js
const a = 'it...';
```

**Reports** at `1:11`.

**After `codelaw fix`:**

```js
const a = 'it\'';
```

#### a tagged template of another language is not read

```toml
[rules."js/string-content".options]
patterns = { "\\\\.\\\\.\\\\." = "…" }
```

```js
const q = sql`select 1...`;
```

**Reports nothing.**

#### an escape is not read

```toml
[rules."js/string-content".options]
patterns = { "\\\\.\\\\.\\\\." = "…" }
```

```js
const a = "a\u002e\u002e\u002e";
```

**Reports nothing.**

### For a group of files

A `[scope.<name>]` gives some files their own setting, applied after `[rules]` — the `tests` scope `codelaw:js/recommended` ships (`**/*.test.*`, `**/*.spec.*`); naming it extends it, so its files stay:

```toml
[scope.tests]
rules = { "js/string-content" = { options = { patterns = { "\\\\.\\\\.\\\\." = "…" } } } }
```

Or switch it off there:

```toml
[scope.tests]
rules = { "js/string-content" = "off" }
```

A scope's `remap` changes whole severities in its files, after everything else: `remap = { error = "warn" }` never fails the run there.

### Warn locally, fail in CI

The `ci` profile runs when `CI` is set; `local` otherwise; `--profile <name>` or `CODELAW_PROFILE` picks one.

```toml
[profile.local.rules]
"js/string-content" = "warn"

[profile.ci.rules]
"js/string-content" = "error"
```

### In `pyproject.toml` or `package.json`

```toml
# pyproject.toml
[tool.codelaw.rules]
"js/string-content" = { severity = "warn", options = { patterns = { "\\\\.\\\\.\\\\." = "…" } } }
```

```json
{
  "codelaw": {
    "rules": {
      "js/string-content": {"severity": "warn", "options": {"patterns": {"\\\\.\\\\.\\\\.": "…"}}}
    }
  }
}
```

### Silence one finding

An inline `codelaw-ignore` always needs a reason; `expires=`, `warn_days=` and `by=` date it ([SR-LINTER](../../../records/0106_linter.md) decision 6).

- **JavaScript:** `// codelaw-ignore js/string-content: <reason>`
- **Dated:** `// codelaw-ignore js/string-content expires=2026-12-31 by=you@example.com: <reason>`

### Keep today's findings, fail on new ones

```bash
codelaw baseline add --rule js/string-content --expires 2026-12-31 --reason "<why>"
```

See [SR-BASELINE](../../../records/0104_baseline-and-deprecations.md).

### See what applies

```bash
codelaw explain js/string-content       # what it wants, why, how to fix
codelaw check --rule js/string-content  # only this rule
codelaw config --print --for <file>     # the resolved setting, and where it came from
```
